title: Strict increase of the Gaussian distribution function
statement: The standard Gaussian distribution function $\Phi$ is strictly increasing: whenever $a,b\in\mathbb R$ and $a<b$, one has $\Phi(a)<\Phi(b)$.
replaced: Let $\Phi(t)=\int_{-\infty}^{t}e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}\,dx$ be the standard Gaussian cumulative distribution function. It is strictly increasing: for every $a,b\in\mathbb R$ with $a<b$, one has $\Phi(a)<\Phi(b)$.
